name: parsel
license_evidence: https://pypi.org/pypi/parsel/1.12.1/json (License-Expression: BSD-3-Clause; LICENSE in wheel and sdist, SHA-256 7c9a5bce33c5cb32fd5b172f6a0bf2691e19ab11b06503eab2d826f5c6dee90d)
input_api: parsel.Selector(body=local XML bytes, type="xml"); Selector.xpath() with get()/getall() for namespace-uri(), local-name(), namespace::*, ancestor-or-self::*, //text(), //comment() and //processing-instruction(), plus Selector.attrib for attributes
documentation_evidence: The Selector API reference documents body as "a bytes or bytearray object" used with encoding instead of text, and type as "html", "json", "xml" or "text"; the usage guide's "Working on XML (and namespaces)" section shows Selector(text=..., type='xml') with register_namespace and namespace-aware XPath.

dependencies.role: prebuilt abi3 extension imported by w3lib.html; not on the XML parse path
Parsel's XML parser binding (lxml.etree.XMLParser); built from sdist
lxml's C XML parser, built from source

scope: Valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 local byte streams without DOCTYPE through Selector(body=bytes, type='xml'): namespace-expanded element and attribute names, namespace declarations (as in-scope changes), decoded text nodes in document order, comments, processing instructions and tree depth read through Parsel's XPath API. CDATA becomes ordinary text (lxml strip_cdata default), the XML declaration is not a node, and Selector strips leading/trailing whitespace and every NUL byte from the body before parsing.
family: Parsel Selector over lxml.etree XMLParser (SafeXMLParser) over libxml2 2.15.4 XML parser
family_note: Not an independent XML tokenizer. Selector(body=bytes, type='xml') strips the body and NUL bytes and calls lxml.etree.fromstring with parsel.selector.SafeXMLParser(recover=True, resolve_entities=False, huge_tree=True, encoding='utf-8'); libxml2 tokenizes and checks the document and builds the lxml tree, and Parsel only wraps that tree in Selector objects for XPath/CSS queries. It shares the lxml/libxml2 parser family with projects/xml/python/lxml and beautifulsoup4 (same lxml 6.1.3 and libxml2 2.15.4 pins), differing in recover=True, huge_tree=True, input stripping and the XPath-based reading of the tree. Scrapy's Selector (lead 'scrapy') is a subclass of this path.
parser_options_caveat: Parsel creates SafeXMLParser(recover=True, encoding='utf-8', huge_tree=True) with resolve_entities=False and calls lxml.etree.fromstring(body, parser=parser, base_url=None). recover=True makes this path lenient where projects/xml/python/lxml uses recover=False; huge_tree=True disables libxml2's size limits; an empty body becomes <html/>, and non-UTF-8 bodies with encoding errors are re-decoded with U+FFFD replacement. None of this was exercised: no malformed, non-UTF-8, DTD or resource inputs were run.
oracle_note: Independent structural oracle: CPython pyexpat (Expat 2.7.4 in the image, not libxml2) in namespace mode computes the same summary from the raw bytes. run-control.py and the feedback check require oracle == Parsel summary on both controls. Expat counts namespace declarations (xmlns="" included); the harness counts in-scope namespace changes against the parent element via XPath namespace::*, so a redundant redeclaration of an in-scope prefix would count only in the oracle. Neither control has one. Text is merged character data, CDATA and decoded references between markup events, stripped, non-empty.

popularity.metric: PyPI Stats last_month downloads excluding known mirrors
popularity.limitation: Package-level downloads, largely pulled in by Scrapy for HTML scraping; the figure does not measure XML parsing or type='xml' use. Rechecked 2026-11-17: last_month 3,699,459, identical to the leads.json entry (lxml 437,507,754 and beautifulsoup4 315,320,831 also unchanged), so the window matches the pilot's other entries.

verification_note: Shared parser family, not an independent XML tokenizer: Parsel's documented Selector(body=bytes, type='xml') hands the stripped bytes to lxml.etree.fromstring with SafeXMLParser(recover=True, resolve_entities=False, huge_tree=True), and libxml2 tokenizes them; Parsel wraps the resulting lxml tree for XPath queries. The pinned image installs parsel 1.12.1 with lxml 6.1.3 linked to source-built libxml2 2.15.4 and asserts that the 'xml' type uses parsel.selector.SafeXMLParser, an lxml.etree.XMLParser subclass. The summary is read only through Selector.xpath()/get() and Selector.attrib. Both valid namespace controls match their expected summaries, which equal the beautifulsoup4 path's, and an independent CPython pyexpat (Expat 2.7.4) oracle in namespace mode produces the same summary for both. The first control executes 100 parsel/selector.py lines and 1,484 libxml2 parser.c lines. The AFL++ bridge maps executed Parsel lines plus parser.c regions: five identical runs of each control yield identical features (940 and 1,039) and AFL++ maps (934 and 1,031 tuples); the second control changes 213 parser.c features and 209 tuple IDs and no Parsel line, so all input-dependent feedback comes from libxml2. parser.c lines 8700-8720 are excluded as in the lxml path. The controls do not establish DTD, external entity, non-UTF-8, XML 1.1, huge-tree or malformed-input (recover=True) behavior. CDATA boundaries and the XML declaration are not kept, and namespace declarations are counted as in-scope changes, so a redundant redeclaration would be missed. The 3,699,459 last-month PyPI downloads are package-level and mostly Scrapy HTML use; they do not measure XML parsing.
